title: Sarma (cabbage rolls)
description: Sour cabbage leaves rolled around rice and minced meat, slowly simmered with smoked ribs. Even better on day two.

steps.text: Separate the sauerkraut leaves carefully. If they taste very sour or salty, rinse them in cold water. With a small knife, shave down the thick part of the stem on each leaf so it rolls easily. Chop the small and torn leaves.
steps.tip: Shave the stem flat instead of cutting it out, so the leaf stays in one piece.

steps: Chop the onion, crush the garlic and dice the bacon. Rinse the rice.
Heat {1 tbsp} of the oil in a pan on medium heat and fry the onion and half the bacon for 5 minutes until soft. Let it cool a little.

steps.text: In a large bowl mix the minced meat, rice, egg, garlic, the fried onion and bacon, {1 tsp} of the paprika and the pepper. Knead with your hand until well mixed.
steps.tip: Do not add salt: the sauerkraut and smoked meat bring plenty.

steps.text: Lay a leaf flat with the stem end towards you. Put a heaped spoon of filling near the stem, fold the stem end over it, fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Repeat until the filling is used up.
steps.tip: Do not overfill, because the rice swells. Roll firmly so the sarma does not open while it cooks.

steps: Cover the bottom of a large pot with half the chopped cabbage. Lay the rolls in tightly, seam side down, in layers, tucking the ribs and the rest of the bacon between them. Add the bay leaves and put the rest of the chopped cabbage on top.

steps.text: Pour in cold water until the rolls are just covered. Bring to a gentle simmer, put the lid on and cook on low for 2 hours.
steps.tip: Never stir sarma, it breaks the rolls. Gently shake the pot now and then instead. Top up with hot water if the level drops below the rolls.

steps.text: Make the zaprška (roux): heat the rest of the oil in a small pan, add the flour and stir on medium heat for 2 minutes until golden. Off the heat, stir in the rest of the paprika, the tomato paste and a ladle of the cooking water until smooth.
steps.tip: Paprika burns easily, which is why it goes in off the heat.

steps.text: Pour it over the sarma, shake the pot to spread it and simmer for 15 minutes more.
steps.tip: Sarma is famous for tasting better every day. It keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well. Serve it with mashed potatoes or bread.

title: Pašticada with gnocchi
description: Dalmatian beef braised for hours in red wine with prunes and vegetables until the sauce is dark, glossy and sweet-sour.

ingredients.note: one piece of topside or silverside

steps.text: The day before if you can, make small deep cuts all over the beef with a thin knife. Cut the bacon into thin strips and the garlic into slices, and push them into the cuts.
steps.tip: This is called špikanje. It keeps the meat juicy during the long cook.

steps.text: Rub the meat with the vinegar, salt and pepper. Cover it and keep it in the fridge overnight, or at least while you chop the vegetables.
steps.tip: Traditionally it marinates in vinegar for a day or more. One night is plenty.

steps.text: Chop the onions, carrots and celeriac. Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot on medium-high and brown the meat well on all sides, about 10 minutes. Take it out.
steps.tip: Take your time: the brown crust flavours the whole sauce.

steps: Turn the heat to medium. Fry the onions, carrots and celeriac in the same pot for 10 minutes, until soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato paste, cloves, nutmeg, bay leaves and prunes and cook for 2 minutes.

steps.text: Put the meat back, pour in the wine and enough water to come halfway up the meat. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook very gently for 2.5 to 3 hours, turning the meat every half hour.
steps.tip: Add a little water whenever the liquid drops below a third of the way up the meat. It is done when a fork slides in with no resistance.

steps.text: Lift out the meat and the bay leaves. Blend the sauce until smooth, then simmer it without a lid until thick and glossy.
steps.tip: Taste it now. A little more vinegar, or a pinch of sugar, balances the sweet and sour.

steps: Slice the meat across the grain into thick slices and warm them in the sauce.

steps.text: Cook the gnocchi in salted water as the packet says. Serve with the meat and plenty of sauce.
steps.tip: Pašticada is best made a day ahead: it slices neatly when cold and the flavour deepens. It keeps 4 days.

title: Grah (bean stew with smoked meat)
description: A thick, warming bean stew with smoked ribs, paprika and bay. A classic Thursday lunch in Croatian homes.
steps: The night before, cover the beans with plenty of cold water and leave them to soak overnight.

steps.text: Drain the beans, put them in a large pot, cover with fresh water and bring to the boil. Pour this first water away.
steps.tip: Throwing away the first water makes the beans easier to digest.

steps.text: Put the beans back in the pot with the ribs, bay leaves and {2500 ml} water. Bring to the boil, then simmer on low with the lid half on for 1 hour.
steps.tip: Do not add salt: the smoked ribs bring enough. Salt added early can keep the beans hard.

steps.text: Dice the carrots and chop the onions. Add the carrots and half the onions to the pot and cook for 40 minutes more, until the beans are soft.
steps.tip: Squash a bean between your fingers: it should be creamy all the way through.

steps: Make the zaprška (roux): heat the oil in a small pan on medium heat and fry the rest of the onion for 5 minutes. Add the flour and stir for 2 minutes until light golden.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and quickly stir in the chopped garlic, paprika and tomato paste. Add a ladle of the bean liquid and stir until smooth.
steps.tip: Paprika burns easily, which is why it goes in off the heat. The ladle of liquid stops lumps when it goes into the stew.

steps: Stir it into the stew and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened. Take out the ribs, cut the meat off the bones and put it back. Season with the pepper and taste for salt.

steps.text: Serve hot with bread.
steps.tip: Grah is even better the next day. It keeps 4 days in the fridge; add a little water when you reheat it.

title: Istrian maneštra
description: Hearty Istrian soup of beans, sweetcorn and potato with a little smoked meat, finished with good olive oil.
steps: The night before, put the beans in a big bowl and cover them with plenty of cold water. Leave them to soak overnight.

steps.text: Drain the beans and put them in a large pot with the smoked ribs, bay leaves and {2500 ml} water. Bring to the boil, then simmer on low for 50 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not add salt yet. The ribs are salty, and salt added early can keep beans hard.

steps: Meanwhile peel the potatoes, carrots and celeriac and dice them into small cubes.
Add the vegetables to the pot and simmer for 25 minutes more, until the beans and vegetables are soft.

steps.text: Make the pešt: chop the bacon, garlic and parsley together on a board until they turn into a paste. Chop the onion.
steps.tip: Pešt is the Istrian secret. Chopping everything together releases the flavours into the bacon fat.

steps: Heat {1 tbsp} of the olive oil in a small pan on medium heat and fry the pešt and onion for 3 minutes, until soft and fragrant.
Stir the pešt and the drained sweetcorn into the soup and simmer for 10 minutes.

steps.text: Lift out the ribs, cut the meat off the bones and put it back in the pot. Taste and add salt if needed. Serve with a drizzle of the rest of the olive oil.
steps.tip: Maneštra is even better the next day. It keeps 4 days in the fridge; add a splash of water when you reheat it.

title: Fiš paprikaš
description: Slavonian fisherman's stew, red with sweet and hot paprika. Made here with white fish fillets and served with noodles.

steps.text: Slice the onions thinly. Cut the fish into large pieces, about 5 cm.
steps.tip: In Slavonia it is made with river fish such as carp or catfish. Hake works well and has fewer bones.

steps.text: Put the onions in a wide pot with the oil and a splash of water. Cook on medium-low with the lid on for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft.
steps.tip: The onions melt into the sauce and thicken it. They should be soft, not brown.

steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika, chili and tomato paste. Pour in the wine and {1000 ml} water and put it back on the heat.
steps.tip: Paprika burns easily, which is why it goes in off the heat.

steps: Bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes.

steps.text: Add the fish and the salt. Simmer gently for 10 minutes without stirring, just shaking the pot now and then.
steps.tip: Stirring breaks the fish into flakes. Shaking keeps the pieces whole.

steps: Meanwhile cook the noodles in salted water as the packet says and drain them.
Serve the noodles in deep plates with the paprikaš ladled over.

title: Čobanac (shepherd's stew)
description: Slavonian mixed-meat stew with lots of onion and paprika, simmered until the meat falls apart.
steps: Cut the beef and pork into 3 cm cubes and pat them dry. Chop the onions and garlic. Slice the carrots and pepper and cut the potatoes into chunks.

steps.text: Melt the lard in a large heavy pot on medium-high. Brown the meat in batches, a few minutes per batch, and set it aside on a plate.
steps.tip: Do not crowd the pot. Meat packed in tightly steams and turns grey instead of browning.

steps: Turn the heat to medium-low and fry the onions slowly for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden.

steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and stir in the garlic, paprika, chili and tomato paste. Add the meat with its juices, the wine, bay leaves, salt and {1500 ml} water.
steps.tip: Paprika burns easily, which is why it goes in off the heat.

steps: Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 1.5 hours, stirring now and then.
Add the carrots, pepper and potatoes and cook for 40 minutes more, until the meat is very tender and the potatoes are soft.

steps.text: Čobanac should be thick like a stew, not a soup. Add a little water if it is too thick, or cook it uncovered for a while if it is thin. Serve with bread.
steps.tip: In Slavonia it is cooked in a kotlić over a fire. It keeps 4 days in the fridge and tastes even better the next day.

title: Stuffed peppers in tomato sauce
description: Peppers filled with rice and minced meat, baked slowly in a light tomato sauce. Served with mashed potato.
steps: Cut the tops off the peppers and pull out the seeds and white ribs. Chop the onion and rinse the rice.
In a bowl mix the meat, rice, onion, egg, paprika, {1 tsp} of the salt and the pepper with your hand until even.

steps.text: Fill the peppers loosely, pressing gently, up to about 1 cm from the top.
steps.tip: Do not pack them tight: the rice swells as it cooks and can split the peppers. Roll any leftover filling into small meatballs and cook them alongside.

steps: Stand the peppers upright in a pot in which they fit snugly. Mix the passata with {300 ml} water, the sugar and a pinch of salt and pour it over.

steps.text: Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 1 hour.
steps.tip: Shake the pot now and then. They are done when the peppers are soft and the rice in the filling is tender.

steps: Meanwhile peel the potatoes, cut them into chunks and boil them in salted water for 20 minutes until soft.

steps.text: Drain the potatoes and mash them with the warm milk, butter and a pinch of salt. Serve with the peppers and plenty of sauce.
steps.tip: They keep 3 days in the fridge and reheat well in their sauce.

title: Grilled sea bream with Swiss chard and potatoes
description: The Dalmatian plate: whole grilled fish with blitva, potatoes, garlic and plenty of olive oil.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C. If the fish are not cleaned, ask at the fish counter to gut and scale them. Rinse them and pat dry.
steps.tip: The fishmonger does this for free, and it saves a lot of mess at home.

steps.text: Make 2 or 3 cuts on each side of the fish. Brush them with {1 tbsp} of the olive oil, season inside and out with half the salt and put a slice of lemon inside each.
steps.tip: The cuts help the heat get in, so the thick part cooks as fast as the tail.

steps.text: Lay the fish on a lined baking tray and roast for 15 to 20 minutes, turning once halfway, until the eyes are white and the flesh comes off the bone easily.
steps.tip: Pull the back fin: if it comes out easily, the fish is done.

steps: Meanwhile peel and cube the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 10 minutes. Wash and chop the chard, add it to the pot and cook for 8 minutes more. Drain well.

steps.text: In the same pot, warm {3 tbsp} of the oil with the sliced garlic on low heat for 1 minute. Add the potatoes and chard and crush them roughly with a fork. Season with the rest of the salt.
steps.tip: This is the classic Dalmatian side dish, blitva. Be generous with the olive oil.

steps: Serve the fish with the chard and potatoes, the rest of the oil drizzled over and the rest of the lemon in wedges.

title: Brudet with polenta
description: Fish stew from the coast, cooked gently in tomato, wine and a little vinegar, with soft polenta on the side.
steps: Slice the onions and chop the garlic and parsley. Clean the squid and cut it into rings. Cut the fish into large pieces.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot on medium heat and soften the onions for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and squid and cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.

steps.text: Add the passata, wine, vinegar, salt, pepper and {200 ml} water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: The vinegar is typical for Dalmatian brudet. It gives a gentle sour note.

steps.text: Lay the fish pieces in the sauce, cover and cook gently for 10 minutes. Do not stir: shake the pot now and then instead.
steps.tip: Stirring breaks up the fish. Shaking the pot is the traditional way.

steps.text: Meanwhile bring {1000 ml} salted water to the boil. Pour in the polenta in a thin stream while whisking, then cook it on low as the packet says, stirring often.
steps.tip: Instant polenta takes a few minutes, traditional much longer. Add a little hot water if it gets too stiff.

steps: Scatter the brudet with parsley and serve it with the polenta.

title: Mussels buzara
description: Mussels steamed open in white wine, garlic and parsley with breadcrumbs to thicken. Bread for dipping is a must.
steps: Put the mussels in a sink of cold water. Scrub each one, pull the hairy beard off towards the hinge and throw away any with broken shells.

steps.text: Tap any open mussels on the side of the sink. Throw away those that do not close within a few seconds.
steps.tip: Open mussels that do not close are dead and not safe to eat.

steps: Chop the garlic and parsley finely.
Warm the olive oil and garlic in a large pot on medium heat for 1 minute, without letting the garlic brown.
Turn the heat to high, add the mussels and wine, put the lid on and cook for 5 minutes, shaking the pot every minute, until the shells have opened.

steps.text: Throw away any mussels that stayed closed. Stir in the parsley, pepper and breadcrumbs and cook for 2 minutes more, until the juices thicken slightly.
steps.tip: The breadcrumbs thicken the sauce, which is typical for buzara.

steps.text: Serve straight from the pot with bread to dip in the sauce.
steps.tip: Use an empty shell as tweezers to pick out the other mussels.

title: Prawn risotto
description: Creamy coastal risotto with prawns, a splash of white wine and lots of parsley.

steps.text: Crumble the stock cube into {1200 ml} hot water in a pot and keep it warm on low heat.
steps.tip: Hot stock keeps the rice cooking evenly. Cold stock stops it every time you add a ladle.

steps: Chop the onion, garlic and parsley. If the prawns are frozen, thaw them in cold water and pat them dry.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan on medium heat and soften the onion and garlic for 5 minutes.

steps.text: Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes, until the grains look a little see-through at the edges.
steps.tip: Toasting the rice first helps it keep a slight bite.

steps: Pour in the wine and stir until it has almost all bubbled away.

steps.text: Add a ladle of hot stock and stir until it is almost absorbed, then add the next. Keep going for 18 minutes, stirring often.
steps.tip: Taste a grain: it should be soft with a tiny bite in the middle. You may not need all the stock.

steps: Add the prawns and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until they are pink.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the butter, parsley and a squeeze of lemon, cover and leave for 2 minutes.
steps.tip: Risotto should flow slowly on the plate, like lava. Add a splash of stock if it is too stiff.

title: Ričet (barley and bean stew)
description: Old-fashioned continental stew of pearl barley, beans and smoked meat. Cheap, filling and freezes well.
steps: The night before, cover the beans with plenty of cold water and leave them to soak overnight.

steps.text: Drain the beans and rinse the barley. Put both in a large pot with the ribs, bay leaves and {2500 ml} water. Bring to the boil, skim off any foam and simmer on low for 1 hour.
steps.tip: Stir now and then: barley likes to stick to the bottom. Do not add salt yet.

steps.text: Dice the carrots, parsnip and potatoes. Add them to the pot and simmer 30 minutes more, until the beans and barley are soft.
steps.tip: Add a little hot water if it gets too thick. Ričet should be thick but still a stew, not a porridge.

steps: Chop the onion and garlic. Fry them in the oil in a small pan on medium heat for 5 minutes until soft, then stir them into the stew.
Lift out the ribs, cut the meat off the bones and put it back. Chop the parsley and stir it in.

steps.text: Taste and season with pepper, and with salt only if it needs it.
steps.tip: Smoked meat is salty. Ričet keeps 4 days and thickens as it stands, so add water when you reheat it.

title: Savoy cabbage stew with sausage
description: Kelj, potatoes and smoked sausage in one pot, thickened the old way with a little fried flour and garlic.
steps: Cut the savoy cabbage (kelj) into quarters, cut out the hard core and shred the leaves. Peel and dice the potatoes.
Put the cabbage and potatoes in a large pot with {1200 ml} water and the Vegeta. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 25 minutes until both are soft.

steps.text: Meanwhile slice the sausages and brown them in a dry frying pan on medium heat for 5 minutes. Add them to the pot.
steps.tip: Browning them first gives the stew a smoky flavour.

steps: Make the zaprška (roux): heat the oil in the same pan and fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes, then add the flour and stir for 2 minutes until light golden.

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, stir in the chopped garlic and paprika, then a ladle of liquid from the pot until smooth. Stir it into the stew.
steps.tip: Paprika burns easily, which is why it goes in off the heat.

steps.text: Simmer for 5 minutes until thickened. Season with the pepper and taste for salt before serving.
steps.tip: Vegeta is already salty, so taste before adding any salt.

title: Breaded chicken with potato salad
description: Crisp breaded chicken fillets with a Slavonian-style warm potato salad dressed with oil, vinegar and onion.

ingredients.note: for frying, some stays in the pan

steps: Wash the potatoes and put them, in their skins, in a pot of cold salted water. Bring to the boil and cook for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily.

steps.text: Drain them and peel them while still warm, holding each one with a fork. Slice them into rounds into a bowl.
steps.tip: Warm potatoes soak up the dressing much better than cold ones.

steps.text: Slice the onion very thinly. Add it to the potatoes with the vinegar, the pumpkin seed oil, half the salt and the pepper. Mix gently and leave to stand.
steps.tip: Pumpkin seed oil (bučino ulje) gives the typical northern Croatian taste. A splash of the warm potato water makes the salad creamier.

steps: Cut the chicken breasts into slices about 1 cm thick, and flatten any thicker pieces with a pan between baking paper. Season with the rest of the salt.

steps.text: Set out three plates: flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs. Coat each piece in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing them on.
steps.tip: Shake off extra flour before the egg. Use one hand for dry and one for wet, so your fingers do not get breaded too.

steps.text: Heat the sunflower oil in a large frying pan on medium-high. Fry the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until golden and cooked through.
steps.tip: The oil is ready when a breadcrumb sizzles at once. Cut the thickest piece to check: it should be white all the way through.

steps: Drain on kitchen paper. Serve with the potato salad and the green salad.

title: Roast chicken legs with potatoes
description: Sunday tray bake: chicken legs roasted on potatoes and onions with rosemary and garlic until crisp.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the potatoes (or leave the skins on) and cut them into wedges. Cut the onions into quarters and chop the garlic.
Toss the potatoes, onions and garlic on a large roasting tray with {2 tbsp} of the olive oil, the rosemary and half the salt, and spread them out.

steps.text: Pat the chicken legs dry and rub them with the paprika and the rest of the salt. Lay them on top of the potatoes, skin side up.
steps.tip: Dry skin gets crisp, and the juices from the chicken drip onto the potatoes and flavour them.

steps.text: Roast for 55 to 60 minutes, until the skin is crisp and golden.
steps.tip: Pierce the thickest part near the bone: the juices should run clear, not pink. Turn the potatoes once halfway if they brown unevenly.

steps.text: While it roasts, shred the cabbage very thinly. Mix it with the vinegar, the rest of the oil and a pinch of salt, and squeeze it with your hands for a moment so it softens.
steps.tip: Made early, the salad gets softer and tastier as it stands.

steps: Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then serve with the potatoes, onions and cabbage salad.

title: Green bean stew with pork
description: Green beans, potato and carrot simmered with small pieces of pork neck and a garlicky roux.
steps: Cut the pork into small cubes and chop the onion and garlic. Top and tail the green beans and cut them in half. Dice the potatoes and carrots.

steps.text: Heat {1 tbsp} of the oil in a large pot on medium-high and brown the pork for 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes more until soft.
steps.tip: If the pot is crowded, brown the meat in two batches so it browns instead of stewing.

steps: Add {1200 ml} water and the Vegeta, bring to the boil and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the green beans, potatoes and carrots and simmer for 20 minutes more, until everything is soft.

steps.text: Make the zaprška (roux): heat the rest of the oil in a small pan, add the flour and stir on medium heat for 2 minutes until light golden. Off the heat, stir in the garlic and paprika, then a ladle of liquid from the pot.
steps.tip: Paprika burns easily, which is why it goes in off the heat.

steps.text: Stir it into the stew and simmer for 5 minutes until thickened. Serve with a spoon of sour cream on each plate if you like.
steps.tip: Taste for salt before serving: Vegeta is already salty.

title: Grilled squid with chard
description: Squid grilled quickly over high heat, dressed with garlic, parsley and lemon, with blitva and potatoes.

steps.text: Clean the squid if needed: pull out the head and the clear quill and rinse the tube inside and out. Cut off the tentacles just below the eyes and keep them.
steps.tip: Ask at the fish counter to clean them for you. Frozen cleaned squid works well too; thaw it in the fridge.

steps: Peel and cube the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 10 minutes. Wash and chop the chard, add it to the pot and cook for 8 minutes more. Drain well.
Dress the potatoes and chard with {2 tbsp} of the olive oil, half the garlic (chopped) and a pinch of the salt, and crush them lightly with a fork. Keep warm.
Mix the rest of the garlic, the chopped parsley, the lemon juice and most of the rest of the oil in a small bowl.

steps.text: Pat the squid very dry, brush it with the last of the oil and season with the rest of the salt.
steps.tip: Dry squid chars nicely. Wet squid steams and turns rubbery.

steps.text: Heat a grill pan or heavy frying pan on high until smoking. Grill the squid for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, pressing it down, until charred in places.
steps.tip: Squid needs either a very short or a very long cook. More than a few minutes on high heat makes it tough.

steps: Slice the tubes into rings, spoon the garlic and parsley oil over and serve with the chard and potatoes.

title: Beef goulash with polenta
description: Tender beef in a rich paprika and onion sauce, spooned over soft polenta. A cold-weather favourite.
steps: Cut the beef into 3 cm cubes and pat them dry. Chop the onions and garlic and grate the carrot.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a heavy pot on medium-high. Brown the beef in batches, a few minutes per batch, and set it aside.
steps.tip: Do not crowd the pot, or the meat steams instead of browning.

steps.text: Turn the heat to medium-low and cook the onions in the same pot for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and sweet.
steps.tip: Plenty of slowly cooked onion is what makes goulash thick and rich.

steps.text: Take the pot off the heat and stir in the garlic, carrot, paprika and tomato paste. Add the beef with its juices, the wine, bay leaves, salt, pepper and {1000 ml} water.
steps.tip: Paprika burns easily, which is why it goes in off the heat.

steps.text: Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 1 hour 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the meat is very tender.
steps.tip: It is done when a cube breaks apart easily with a spoon. Add a little water if it gets too thick.

steps.text: Near the end, bring {1400 ml} salted water to the boil. Pour in the polenta in a thin stream while whisking, then cook on low as the packet says, stirring often.
steps.tip: Add a little hot water if the polenta gets too stiff.

steps.text: Serve the goulash over the polenta.
steps.tip: Goulash keeps 4 days in the fridge and tastes even better the next day.

title: Potato moussaka
description: Layers of potato and seasoned minced meat baked under an egg and milk topping. Popular all over Croatia.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the potatoes and slice them thinly, about 3 mm. Chop the onions.
steps.tip: The slicing side of a grater makes thin, even slices fast.

steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan on medium heat and fry the onions for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the mince, paprika, half the salt and the pepper. Cook for about 8 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and crumbly.

steps.text: Grease a baking dish. Layer the potatoes and meat, starting and ending with potatoes, and sprinkle each potato layer with a little of the rest of the salt.
steps.tip: Three layers of potato and two of meat works well.

steps: Pour {200 ml} of the milk over, cover the dish with foil and bake for 40 minutes.

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sour cream and the rest of the milk. Take off the foil, pour this over the top and bake uncovered for 20 minutes more, until golden and set.
steps.tip: Push a knife through the middle: the potatoes should be soft all the way down.

steps.text: Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting, so it holds together. Serve with a cucumber salad.
steps.tip: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Reheat portions in the oven or microwave.
